title: Aloo Baingan
subtitle: A north Indian dry curry of potato and aubergine
excerpt: Aloo means potato, baingan means aubergine. Both are fried first so they hold their shape in the spiced sauce. The finished dish is mostly dry, with a deep, earthy flavour.
sourceNotes: North Indian home-cook tradition; a staple across Punjab and Uttar Pradesh.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be made a few hours ahead and reheated gently in the pan with a splash of water.

content.text: Aloo baingan is a dry north Indian vegetable curry with deep, savoury flavour. Frying the aubergine and potato before they go into the spice base is what gives the dish its character. Do not skip this step or the vegetables will go mushy.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wide pan over high heat. Add the aubergine cubes and fry for 5 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden on most sides. Remove and set aside.
Add another tablespoon of oil. Fry the potato cubes over medium-high heat for 6 minutes until the edges are golden. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining oil. Add the mustard seeds and cumin seeds. When they pop and sizzle, add the onion. Fry over medium heat for 6 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the garlic and ginger. Stir for one minute. Add the turmeric, coriander, and chilli powder. Stir for 30 seconds.
Add the tinned tomatoes. Cook for 8 minutes, stirring, until the sauce is thick and the oil separates at the edges. Season with salt.
Return the potato to the pan. Stir gently to coat. Add 80ml of water, cover, and cook for 5 minutes until the potato is cooked through.
Add the aubergine. Stir gently, sprinkle over the garam masala, and cook uncovered for 3 minutes. Scatter over fresh coriander and serve.

items.symptom: The aubergine has broken apart into a mush.
items.cause: It was stirred too often while frying, or added to the sauce too early.
items.fix: Add the aubergine in the final 3 minutes only. Handle it gently and do not stir more than twice.

items.symptom: The potato is still hard in the middle.
items.cause: The cubes were too large, or the lid was lifted too early.
items.fix: Keep the cubes to 2cm and keep the lid on for the full 5 minutes once the water is added.

items.cause: The aubergine was not fried at a high enough heat and absorbed too much oil before browning.
items.fix: Make sure the oil is very hot before the aubergine goes in. High heat sears the outside quickly so less oil is absorbed.
